parser: a `unique if … else if` chain in procedural code reports its no-match (§3.b unique-if-chain)

§4.5.585 — ROADMAP §5.2 row 1, §3.b unique-if-chain (the external report;
§4.5.583's attempt, reverted until §2 🆕 Z closed in §4.5.584). Oracles:
verilator 5.052 --binary --timing --assert, run with
+verilator+error+limit+1000 (the oracle for `unique if`; silent on every
`priority if`; no oracle for x, order or counts); iverilog 13.0 -g2012
(rejects `unique if`; the oracle on the `unique case` twins and on order).

Bug: `parse_unique_priority` (hdl-parser/src/assertions.rs) armed the
no-match report only on a first `if` with no `else`, so
`unique if (a) … else if (b) …` with no final `else` reported nothing when
no condition held, where verilator reports `'unique if' statement violated`
at the first `if`'s line.

The rule:
- The arm goes on the last `if` of the `else if` series and reports at the
  first `if`'s span. The series is decided from the written tokens, never
  the node kind: `parse_if` (stmt_ctl.rs) records in `Parser.else_if_at`
  the span.lo of an `If` parsed right after `else` when the next token is a
  bare `if` (attributes are stripped by the lexer). An immediate assert /
  assume after `else` desugars to `Stmt::If` too (assertions.rs, its span
  starts at the `assert` token) and ends the series, as does a begin…end, a
  label, a delay / event / wait control, `;` or a `case`. A qualified
  `unique|priority|unique0|priority0 if` after `else` is the series' final
  `else` statement (IEEE 1800-2017 Syntax 12-2) and reports only by its own
  qualifier.
- Every function and task body keeps PRE's lone-`if` rule: `tf_body`
  (functask.rs, the one body parser behind `parse_function_def` and
  `parse_task_def`) sets `first_if_arm_only`. Armed: initial, always,
  always_ff, always_comb, always_latch, final and the fork branches inside
  them. Three measured reasons hold the arm back in subroutine bodies:
  the constant-function interpreter refuses a call that reaches the arm
  (E3009 where both oracles fold; §3.b unique-const-fn); a continuous assign
  runs the function it calls once more at t0 on x, before the initial that
  writes its inputs, and that run reaches whatever the function calls (a
  class method through a handle, a void method through `this.`, a
  constructor through `new`, a formal-less item `function void`), so an
  armed miss there reports at t0 where both oracles are silent (§2 🆕 AB,
  new); and the package-scoped call closure walk treats the synthesized
  report as impure and refuses a legal `pk::f(…)` (§3.b unique-pkg-closure,
  new). Each narrowing by declaration kind (class functions, then void
  methods and constructors, then formal-less void functions) met the next
  route in grounding, planning and review round 1, so the axis was cut at
  the subroutine boundary instead.

No AST, IR or format change (format_version 35). A design without a
procedural `if` chain parses to the identical .vu (a design with chains in
every subroutine kind: PRE .vu = POST .vu; the 11 corpus workloads' vcmp
snapshots are byte-identical; no bench source has a `unique` / `priority`
`if`).

Measured (PRE = 75f255d4 release, POST = this commit; native = interp =
vm, staged vcmp -> velab -> vrun, JIT with VITA_JIT=1, product build
--no-default-features):
- 396 cells: 118 verilator report lines gained in 67 cells (the external
  report's repro included); no PRE report lost; no output change other than
  W4031 lines; run.json routes and --obs-procs process counts identical; VCD
  identical; JIT equal to native.
- Reports POST adds at t0: a consumer-first always_comb chain (§2 🆕 AA, a
  recorded split, now reached by chains too), a self-timed `always` written
  before its driving initial (vita = iverilog's source order; verilator
  starts the initial first: a new oracle-split line), and cells where
  verilator also reports at t0 (initial first, program initial, an x
  register).
- Left silent where verilator reports (vita = PRE): chains in function and
  task bodies; an outer series whose `else` is a qualified `if` (verilator
  continues through `else unique0 if`; IEEE ends it there). An inner
  `unique if` after `else` reports at its own line where verilator names the
  outer one (IEEE gives the miss to the inner statement; PRE the same for a
  lone inner `if`). `priority if` chains report (hand-IEEE §12.4.2).

Review: 2 rounds, differential + soundness lenses.
- Round 1, two BLOCKING: `priority if … else unique0 if` reported where
  verilator, IEEE and PRE are silent (fixed: only a bare `if` continues the
  series); a formal-less item `function void` called by a function reached
  from a continuous assign reported at t0 (q6a, net-declaration, port,
  interface and package variants) — the third §2 🆕 AB route found after two
  narrowings, so subroutine bodies were cut out whole. Also round 1: a
  package-scoped call reaching an armed void function was newly refused
  (closed by the same cut; root recorded as unique-pkg-closure).
- Round 2 (delta): both lenses PASS (314 + 365 cells; flag census: 3
  writers, 1 reader, no return or procedural-block parse inside `tf_body`).

Tests: crates/cli/tests/unique_if_chain.rs (verilator text above every
pin; residue pins for subroutine bodies, qualified `else`, the t0 split
cells), crates/hdl-parser/tests/unique_if_chain_shape.rs. Mutants killed:
the walk removed; the flag unset in task bodies; a qualified `if`
recorded; the else_if_at check dropped.

Docs: manual 006 §1.4 (the rule and its residues) and a §3.1 row (a
continuous assign's extra t0 run; workaround `always_comb y = f(a, b);`),
manual 003, CHANGELOG.

Out of scope (queued): §2 🆕 AB; §3.b unique-pkg-closure; the
subroutine-body residue stays in unique-if-chain (BLOCKED on both and on
unique-const-fn); unique-if-text (W4031 says `case statement`);
unique-overlap-note. PROBE_CATALOG: vita accepts a function that calls a
task (both tools refuse, IEEE §13.4).
